summary: Reviewed git diff origin/development...HEAD (70 files) for climb-recording share SEO. No critical findings. AC-1–AC-40 production units match architecture.md: additive recordClimb.runId; anonymous POST has no runId; parseRecordingId max 32 is compatible with Prisma cuid() (25 chars); payload is an allow-list DTO with handle redaction; validateShareFieldLength returns {valid,length,limit} only; ShareRun after save and dashboard copy/watch use /r/{id}; getPlayPageMetadata takes no token and does not import decodeRunReplay; /b/[slug] generateMetadata calls notFound() on unknown slug; middleware imports isBot (tiktok/bytespider/bytedance) and matcher still excludes /r/; sitemap emits /, /play, /climb, /b/{slug} with zero /r/ paths; JSON-LD is WebPage only. Did not fail for stale landing AC-27/AC-32 comments. react.cache module-load is a warning (Next compiled React exports cache; vitest's react 18.3.1 does not). nextStage qa-acceptance.
goal: SEO for sharing climb-recording links on X, TikTok, and YouTube so a marketing agent can post them and crawlers unfurl a unique preview (title, description, image, canonical URL) per recording.

findings.issue: getClimbRunRow = cache(...) runs at module load. npm react@18.3.1 (vitest node, default export) does not export cache, so any unmocked import of climb.ts throws TypeError. Next.js 15 serves next/dist/compiled/react, which does export cache, so App Router pages and node route handlers that import climb.ts (POST /api/climb/result, dashboard, recording OG, share JSON, /r/{id}, landing, /climb) are fine in production. Tests already identity-mock react.cache. Not a production 500, but the module is now unloadable outside Next without a mock.
findings.fix: Guard at init: const memo = typeof cache === 'function' ? cache : <T extends (...args: never[]) => unknown>(fn: T) => fn; then getClimbRunRow = memo(async (id) => ...). Do not rely on vitest mocks for production module load.

findings.issue: buildDashboardShareUrl is the named AC-29 unit and is imported only by app/tests/share/dashboard.test.ts. ClimbReplaysSection uses buildDashboardShareActions (copy URL is payload.canonicalUrl) and a relative Watch href `/r/${run.id}`. Dashboard behaviour is correct (/r/{id}, not /play?r=), but the named builder has no non-test caller (kernel gate 4).
findings.fix: Call buildDashboardShareUrl from ClimbReplaysSection for the copy/watch URL, or inline it into buildDashboardShareActions and stop exporting a tests-only helper.

findings.issue: AC-40 is proven structurally (middleware config.matcher has no /r/; generateMetadata has no auth). There is still no in-process document GET of /r/{id} with Twitterbot/Bytespider against a live Next server. Spec AC-40 wants HTTP 200 for those UAs; architecture says the matcher exclusion plus a public page is the unit.
findings.fix: Optional for qa-acceptance: one live GET of a valid /r/{id} with Twitterbot and Bytespider UAs. Do not block merge on the missing e2e.

feedback.message: Guard react.cache at module init in climb.ts so node/vitest importers do not throw. Production Next compiled React already provides cache.
feedback.action: const memo = typeof cache === 'function' ? cache : identity; getClimbRunRow = memo(async (id) => ...).

learnings.insight: react@18.3.1's default CJS export (app/node_modules/react, used by vitest) does not include cache. Next.js 15.5 compiles server modules against next/dist/compiled/react, which does export cache. A TypeError: cache is not a function in vitest therefore does not prove a production crash of POST /api/climb/result or /r/{id}. It does prove climb.ts cannot be imported from node without a mock.
learnings.action: When wrapping a Prisma loader in react.cache inside a file also imported by route handlers and unit tests, guard typeof cache === 'function' at module init. Do not treat the vitest TypeError as a merge-blocking production defect without checking next/dist/compiled/react.

learnings.insight: parseRecordingId's ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$ cap (32 chars) is the architecture allow-list, not a Prisma-length bug. ClimbRun.id @default(cuid()) is CUID1 (25 lowercase [a-z0-9]). Lowercasing before findUnique matches stored ids. A 33-char fixture must 404; a real cuid must pass.
learnings.action: Do not widen the parser to 36/uuid or treat 32 vs 25 as a mismatch. If the schema ever switches to uuid() or cuid(2) with a longer custom length, change parseRecordingId in the same commit as the schema.

learnings.insight: Reviewer classified 0 critical, 2 warnings, 1 info on origin/development...HEAD (70 files, 5034+/243-). Warnings: react.cache module load (test/node only); buildDashboardShareUrl tests-only export. AC-1–AC-40 production wiring holds. Landing AC-27/AC-32 comments not failed.
